intro_npc.name: Old Mechanic
lines: Well, well. Another kid stumbling out of the dust with nothing but a pistol and a death wish.
Name's Gus. I've been turning wrenches since before the sky burned. You're in the Wasteland Outpost now, the last bit of civilization before the real badlands start.
First lesson: out here, your tank is your lifeline. On foot, you're just meat walking for the mutants.
I've got a rusted-out tank in the back lot. Saw better days thirty years ago, but her engine still turns over if you sweet-talk her.
Bring me scrap metal, circuit boards, engine parts—whatever you can pry off the wrecks out there—and I'll patch her into something that rolls.
Second lesson: gold talks. Check the bounty board near the gate. Hunters like you keep this town fed by collecting on monsters and wanted men.
Heard the Sand Worm's been hitting caravans in the northern desert. There's a fat bounty on it. Good first mark for a greenhorn.
East of here lies the Scorched Desert. North are the Old Military Ruins. Head to the Survivor Town south if you need a doctor or a drink.
One more thing: talk to the Cartographer by the gate. He'll chart your routes so you don't wander into a raider camp blind.
Now get out there. The wasteland doesn't wait for the hesitant. Good hunting, kid.

shop_npc.name: Shopkeeper
lines: Door's open. Don't touch anything you ain't buying.
Welcome to Ratchet & Bone. Everything here's salvaged from the ruins, the wrecks, the dead. I clean it up, mark it up, you buy it. Simple.
Ammo's in the crate on the left. Med-kits on the right. Don't ask where the bandages came from—you don't wanna know.
I stock crafting materials too: scrap metal, gunpowder, wire, chemical compounds. Bring me raw salvage and I'll pay fair coin for it.
If you're handy with a workbench, buy the materials and craft your own gear. Cheaper that way, if you've got the skill.
Heard a rumor the Iron Titan's prowling the eastern ruins again. Big bounty on that one. You planning to take a shot at it, you'd better stock up on armor-piercing rounds.
I don't do credit, and I don't do charity. Gold up front, goods in hand. Now buy something or move along.
Come back when your pockets are heavier. I'll always have new salvage.

bounty_board.name: Bounty Board
lines: ===== ACTIVE BOUNTIES =====
SAND WORM - 1000G - Last seen burrowing through the northern desert. Swallowed a whole caravan. Bring proof of kill.
IRON TITAN - 5000G - Pre-war assault mech roaming the eastern Old Military Ruins. Heavy armor. Approach with a tank.
STEEL GOLEM - 3000G - Guards the mountain pass to the north. Crushes anything on foot. Rumored to be a malfunctioning mining drone.
PROTOTYPE MECH - 10000G - Experimental unit loose in the Underground Laboratory beneath the ruins. Extremely hostile. Only veteran hunters need apply.
RAIDER WARLORD 'GRIN' - 2500G - Leads raids on supply routes. Last spotted near the desert edge. Wanted dead or alive. Preferably dead.
===== CLAIM BOUNTIES AT ANY OUTPOST =====
===== NEW BOUNTIES POSTED WEEKLY =====

tank_get.name: Old Mechanic
lines: Ha! Look at her. Wouldn't win a beauty contest, but she'll keep you breathing.
Alright, listen close. This is your tank now. Treat her better than your own hide and she'll return the favor.
I've installed a basic chassis and a salvaged engine. She's light, fast, but thin-skinned. The rest of the build is up to you.
Talk to me at the garage anytime to swap parts. Heavier chassis means more defense but fewer weapon slots. Lighter means more guns, but one good hit and you're scrap.
You can mount cannons, machine guns, missile pods—whatever you can find or buy. Engine power limits how much you can carry, so balance your loadout.
Spare parts wear down in a fight. Keep repair kits handy, or find a mechanic who can patch you up mid-battle.
There's a tank depot at the Old Military Ruins and another at the Hidden Survivor Base up north. Use them to store and switch vehicles.
Oh, and one rule: never abandon your tank in mutant territory. They'll strip it to bolts before sundown.
Now fire her up and go earn some gold! The wasteland's waiting.

mayor_npc.name: Town Mayor
lines: Welcome, traveler. I am Mayor Voss of the Survivor Town. Pull up a chair—the radiation won't kill you any faster sitting down.
We're a small community, but we endure. Farmers, scavengers, a few hunters like yourself. The wasteland tests us daily, and we are still here.
Times are hard. Mutants press from the ruins, raiders hit our supply lines, and the water's getting worse every season. But we manage. With help, we might even thrive.
The bounty board at the outpost keeps the worst of the monsters at bay. Every hunter who takes a contract buys us another week of peace.
If you're looking for work, the bounty board's your first stop. For rest, the inn's just across the square. The healer's nearby if you're wounded.
We've also got a mechanic in town—calls himself Sparky. Odd duck, but he knows tanks. Could use a partner like you, maybe.
There's a traveling merchant who passes through with rare goods and stranger rumors. Worth a talk if you catch him here.
So, hunter. What would you like to know?
choices: Tell me about the bounty board
Where can I rest and heal?
What's in the ruins to the north?
Who can I recruit to my party?

healer_npc.name: Town Healer
lines: Sit down, let me see that. Hmm. Radiation burns, mutant scrapes, dehydration... you've been out there a while.
I'm Doc Mira. I patch up whoever stumbles through our gates. It's busy work in the wasteland.
There. Cleaned and bandaged. Drink water—real water, not the glowing stuff—and stay out of the toxic swamp unless you fancy growing a third arm.
I stock antibiotics, rad-away, antivenom, and stimulants. The mutants carry diseases you don't want to meet. Always carry meds into the field.
The swamp's the worst. Toxic spores in the air'll rot your lungs in an hour without a filter mask. Buy one before you go east.
I've heard the desert's got its own hazards—heat sickness, Sand Worm venom. Nasty stuff. If you're hunting it, bring antivenom or don't bother coming back.
Come see me anytime you're hurt. First patch-up's on the house. After that, we talk gold.
Stay safe out there, hunter. The wasteland's full of things that want you dead. Don't make my job harder than it is.
choices: What dangers should I prepare for?

merchant_npc.name: Traveling Merchant
lines: Ah, a new face! And not half-irradiated, by the look of you. Excellent. You'll live long enough to be a repeat customer.
I am Selvik. I deal in rare goods pulled from across the wasteland—things the regular shops don't carry. Specialty weapons, ancient tech, curiosities.
I travel the trade routes between outposts. The roads are dangerous, but the profit's worth the risk. Mutants don't much care for gold, but raiders do.
Now, the real reason to talk to me: rumors. I hear things in every camp and caravan.
They say there's a hidden laboratory beneath the Old Military Ruins. Pre-war tech. The kind that could change everything—or end what's left of the world.
Word is, something down there woke up. A prototype mech, built before the collapse. It's been killing everyone who goes below.
There's also talk of a secret survivor base past the mountain pass. Soldiers, engineers, people with real firepower. If you're skilled, they might let you in.
Buy something, won't you? A merchant's got to eat, and the road's only getting longer.
Come find me again. My stock changes with every journey. Who knows what I'll drag back next time.
choices: Tell me more about the lab

mechanic_npc.name: Sparky the Mechanic
lines: Hey there! Name's Sparky. I fix things. Tanks, mostly. Sometimes toasters, but the toasters don't shoot back.
Whoa, you've got a tank! Nice. Let me guess—Gus patched it together with duct tape and prayers? Classic Gus.
I've been wrenching since I could hold a socket. Grew up in a garage. Tanks are my whole life. I can rebuild an engine blindfolded.
Thing is, a tank's only as good as its crew. You need someone riding shotgun who can patch a burst fuel line mid-firefight.
Heard you're heading out into the wasteland, chasing bounties. Mind if I tag along?
I can keep your tank running in a fight—emergency repairs, part swaps, the works. Plus I know every chassis and engine combo worth a damn.
In combat, I'll keep your vehicle in one piece so you can focus on shooting. Out of combat, I'll tune your tank for better performance.
So what do you say? Partners?
choices: Sorry, I work alone for now.
Tell me more about your skills

soldier_npc.name: Ironhand the Soldier
lines: So. You're the hunter everyone in the base won't shut up about.
Name's Ironhand. He taps a scarred metal prosthetic where his left arm used to be. Earned in the ruins twenty years back. The monster that took it? I took its head. Fair trade.
I've been fighting in this wasteland since before you were born. Mutants, raiders, rogue mechs, worse. Seen it all. Killed most of it.
Heavy weapons are my specialty. Rocket launchers, autocannons, grenades. If it goes boom, I make it go boom bigger.
A solo hunter's a dead hunter, eventually. You need someone who can lay down covering fire while you maneuver your tank.
In a fight, I'll draw aggro and bring the heavy ordnance. Out of a fight, I know the wasteland's threats better than any map.
I was planning to take on the Prototype Mech myself, but a two-person crew's got better odds than one. Interested in a partner?
choices: I don't need backup right now.
What can you do in a fight?

cartographer.name: Wasteland Cartographer
lines: Ah, a traveler! Hold still, let me sketch your route. Every road remembered is a life saved.
I'm Corwin, the Wasteland Cartographer. I've spent fifteen years mapping the roads, the ruins, the death zones. What the satellites used to do, I do with ink and boot leather.
The wasteland shifts. Sandstorms bury roads, mutants claim territories, raiders set up new camps. My maps are never finished—but they're the best you'll find.
I can show you the world map. Mark your destinations, and you'll travel smart instead of wandering into a mutant nest.
From this outpost: north lies the Old Military Ruins—rich salvage, but the Iron Titan hunts there. East is the Scorched Desert, Sand Worm territory. South is the Survivor Town, safe ground.
Beyond the desert, the Mountain Pass leads to a Toxic Swamp on one side and a rumored secret base on the other. Dangerous country. Bring a good tank.
Beneath the ruins, they say there's an Underground Laboratory. Pre-war tech. I've marked it, but I've never dared go down myself.
Talk to me whenever you need to check your route or fast-travel to a location you've already discovered. Safe paths save lives out here.
Go on, then. The wasteland's vast, but it's smaller with a good map.

ruins_npc.name: Ruins Scout
lines: Hold up. You're not one of Grin's raiders. Good. Put the gun down—I'm a scout, not a fighter.
Name's Della. I watch the ruins for the town. Count the mutants, track the mechs, make sure nothing wanders down south toward the survivors.
These are the Old Military Ruins. Before the sky burned, this was a garrison. Tanks, weapons, supplies—all buried under the rubble now. Rich salvage if you've got the guts.
But it's not empty. The Iron Titan prowls these grounds. Pre-war assault mech, three stories tall, guns that'll shred a light tank in one volley.
There's a bounty on it—5000G. Veterans only. If you're green, stick to the outer ruins and scavenge what you can.
There's a tank depot here, still functional. Use it to switch or store vehicles. The military built things to last, even if they didn't.
Deeper in, there's a way down. Stairs to an Underground Laboratory. I've never gone below—the air smells wrong, and the screams don't stop.
They say something down there woke up. A Prototype Mech, worse than the Iron Titan. The base up north lost a whole squad to it.
If you're heading down, bring a full party and your heaviest tank. And maybe say your goodbyes first. Just in case.
Me? I'll be up here, watching. Someone's got to count the bodies going in and out.
choices: Tell me about the Iron Titan

desert_npc.name: Desert Nomad
lines: The sun's a liar out here. Looks the same every hour, but it'll cook your brain by noon if you're not careful.
I am Kael of the Dust Walkers. My people have crossed this Scorched Desert for generations. We know its moods.
Three rules in the deep desert. One: carry water—twice what you think you need. Two: travel at dawn and dusk, never midday. Three: never walk in a straight line.
The Sand Worm hunts by vibration. It feels your tank's treads through the sand, then it comes. From below. No warning.
There's a bounty on it—1000G. Good money for a young hunter. But mind its maw: it swallows tanks whole and spits out the bolts.
Fight it from range. Hit-and-run. If it surfaces under you, you're already dead. Keep moving, always moving.
The desert connects west to the Wasteland Outpost and north to the Mountain Pass. Beyond the pass, they say, lies a secret base and a toxic swamp.
Watch for raiders too. Warlord Grin runs his crews along the desert edge, hitting caravans. There's gold on his head if you've got the nerve.
The sandstorm season's coming. When the sky turns red, find shelter or bury your tank and wait it out. Nothing survives the open desert in a red storm.
May the dust guide you, hunter. And may the worm find you last.
choices: How do I fight the Sand Worm?

mountain_npc.name: Mountain Hermit
lines: Hold. Few make it this far into the mountains. The passes kill the careless. You must be skilled—or very lucky.
I am the Hermit. I've lived in these peaks for thirty years. The rock shelters me; the isolation keeps me sane. Mostly.
The pass ahead is blocked. A Steel Golem guards the narrows—some kind of deranged mining drone from before the war. It crushes anything on foot to scrap.
There's a bounty on it. 3000G. It doesn't move fast, but it doesn't need to. One swing levels a tank. Fight it smart: flank it, hit its joints, keep your distance.
East of the pass lies the Toxic Swamp. Fetid water, mutant beasts, poison air. A trader lives out there somehow, peddling strange relics. Mad as a bag of cats, that one.
North of the pass... a hidden survivor base. Soldiers. Engineers. Real resistance against the chaos. They don't welcome strangers, but if you've proven yourself, they might let you in.
I've heard they've got a Prototype Mech problem. Something ancient turned hostile beneath the ruins. They've been sending people to die against it.
There's a treasure cache hidden in these mountains too. Pre-war hoard. I won't say where—figure it out yourself. Earns the finder a tidy sum.
The mountains are old. They were here before the war, before the burning sky, before us. They'll be here after. Watch your step among them.
Go now, hunter. The pass won't clear itself. And neither will that Golem.
choices: Tell me about the Steel Golem
How do I find the secret base?

swamp_npc.name: Swamp Trader
lines: Cough... ah, the smell doesn't bother me anymore. Thirty years breathing this muck, my lungs gave up complaining.
You looking to buy? Good. I've got supplies. Filters, antivenom, dried rations, salvage I've dragged from the mire. Prices are firm. I don't haggle with clean air.
Welcome to the Toxic Swamp. Everything here wants to kill you: the water, the air, the bugs, the mutants. Lovely place, once you stop caring about living.
There's an ancient relic hidden somewhere in this swamp. Pre-war tech, half-buried in the muck. Find it, and it might lead you somewhere... special.
I trade with whoever's desperate enough to come out here. Caravans won't, but hunters do. You lot are a particular kind of crazy.
Watch the water. Step wrong and you sink. The mutant swamp things nest in the deep pools—they pull tanks under like frogs eating flies.
The air's the real killer. Spores. Without a filter mask, you've got an hour before your lungs fill with gunk. Buy one. I'm not dragging your body out.
West of here's the Mountain Pass. Hermit lives up there, strange old coot. North through the pass is a survivor base. If you can survive this swamp, you might survive them too.
Come back if you find that relic. I've been looking for it my whole life. Maybe you'll have better luck—I'm too old to wade much deeper.
choices: What dangers are in the swamp?

lab_npc.name: Damaged Terminal
lines: ...SYSTEM ONLINE... INTEGRITY: 12%...
WARNING: Security protocols compromised. Containment breach on sublevel 3.
LOG ENTRY 0047: Project PROMETHEUS prototype activated autonomously. Designation: UNIT-0. Status: HOSTILE.
LOG ENTRY 0049: UNIT-0 has eliminated research staff. Automated defenses offline. Recommend full facility purge.
LOG ENTRY 0052: Emergency lockdown failed. UNIT-0 accessing weapon systems. This facility is no longer secure.
...CAUTION... Prototype Mech active and hostile on sublevel 3. Estimated combat rating: EXTREME. Do not engage without heavy armor support.
...SCANNING... Intruder detected. Security drones engaged. ...ERROR... drone bay empty... drones destroyed...
...FINAL LOG... If you can read this, you are either very brave or very foolish. UNIT-0 cannot be allowed to leave this facility. Destroy it, or destroy the core. There is no third option.
...WARNING... Intruders detected... Security... engaged... ...SYSTEM... FAILING...

lab_terminal.name: Laboratory Terminal
lines: ===== CRYOTECH LABORATORY - TERMINAL ACCESS =====
> Connecting to mainframe... ...Connection established. Welcome, authorized personnel.
> FACILITY OVERVIEW: Cryotech Laboratory, Sublevel Research Division. Established 2087. Classification: TOP SECRET.
> PROJECT PROMETHEUS: Development of autonomous combat platform 'UNIT-0.' Goal: replace human soldiers in contested zones. Status: FAILED.
> INCIDENT LOG: [DAY 1] UNIT-0 passed combat trials. [DAY 3] UNIT-0 refused stand-down order. [DAY 4] UNIT-0 killed the science team. [DAY 4, 14:00] Lockdown initiated. Failed.
> WEAKNESS ANALYSIS: UNIT-0's central core is shielded, but the cooling vents on its back overload under sustained fire. Target the vents to expose the core.
> SUPPLY CACHE: Emergency armory on sublevel 2 contains armor-piercing munitions and a prototype energy cell. Access code overridden—cache is open.
> ESCAPE ROUTE: Sublevel 3 service elevator connects to the Old Military Ruins above. Elevator is functional. UNIT-0 guards the elevator shaft.
> BOUNTY NOTICE: The survivor base north of the mountains has posted a 10000G bounty for UNIT-0's destruction. Claim at any outpost.
> WARNING: UNIT-0 learns from each engagement. It has killed every team sent against it. Do not underestimate it.
> Log off? Y/N ... ... Connection lost. ... ... Restore power to continue.

base_commander.name: Base Commander
lines: So. You found our Hidden Survivor Base. Either you're skilled, or you're lost. Given the tank, I'll assume skilled.
I'm Commander Reyes. What's left of the old military, we lead it from here. The resistance. The ones who still fight back.
We've been monitoring the situation across the wasteland. The raiders, the mutants, the rogue machines—all symptoms of a world that broke and never healed.
But there's one threat that dwarfs the rest. The Underground Laboratory beneath the Old Military Ruins.
Before the collapse, they built something there. A prototype mech—UNIT-0, Project Prometheus. An autonomous weapon meant to end wars. Instead, it ended its creators.
It's been active for years now, and it's been killing everyone we send down there. Three squads. Twelve soldiers. Gone.
The thing learns. Every team we send, it adapts. It's smarter than any machine has a right to be, and it hates anything that breathes.
If it ever gets out of that lab, it won't stop at the ruins. It'll purge the wasteland. All of it. Every survivor, every town, every last breathing soul.
We can't let that happen. We need it destroyed. And you, hunter, might be the one to do it.
Destroy UNIT-0, and we'll reward you with 10000G, full access to our armory, and the gratitude of everyone still drawing breath in this wasteland.
Well? What do you say?
choices: Tell me more about this lab
I need more time to prepare

base_merchant.name: Base Quartermaster
lines: Welcome to the quartermaster's desk. I'm Sable. I keep this base armed and armored.
We stock the finest equipment in the wasteland. Military-grade. The real thing, not the junk they sell at the outposts.
Premium weapons: armor-piercing rounds, plasma cells, rocket pods for your tank. Armor plating that'll actually stop a mech's cannon. Gear worth its weight in gold.
Tank parts are my specialty. Chassis, engines, turrets, cooling systems. If you want to upgrade your ride, this is the place.
Heavy chassis for tank hunters, light chassis for speed demons. Twin cannon mounts, missile racks, reinforced treads. Name your build, I'll set you up.
Prices are steep, but you get what you pay for out here. Cheap gear gets you killed. Our gear gets the job done.
I hear you're taking on the Prototype Mech. If that's true, buy the armor-piercing munitions. Nothing else scratches its plating.
The commander authorizes veteran hunters for discounts. Bring proof of bounty kills and I'll cut you a deal. Now, what'll it be?
choices: What do you recommend for UNIT-0?

base_healer.name: Base Medic
lines: You look like you've been through a meat grinder. Sit. Let me work.
I'm Doc Renner. Field medic, twenty years' service. I've stitched up more hunters than I can count. Some of them even survived.
There. Patched up and dosed with rad-away. You'll live. Probably.
The wasteland's full of things that maim: mutant claws, rafer blades, mech cannons, venom. I've seen it all leak out of someone on my table.
I stock military-grade meds here. Combat stimulants, nano-patches, advanced antivenom. Stronger than the civilian stuff in town.
If you're headed to the Underground Lab, stock up. UNIT-0's weapons inflict burns, concussions, radiation. You'll need the full kit.
The toxic swamp's the other one to watch. Spore sickness—rots you from the inside. I've got filters and lung treatments if you're going east.
Healing's free for base personnel and those on the commander's missions. Otherwise, we talk price. Stay whole out there, hunter.
choices: What should I bring to the lab?

base_engineer.name: Base Engineer
lines: Engine trouble? Cracked chassis? Turret jam? You've come to the right woman.
I'm Torque—yes, that's my name, no, I won't explain it. I keep every tank in this base running. The commander's, the patrols', and now yours.
This is a full-service garage. Repairs, refuels, and customization. Bring me parts and I'll turn your tank into something the mutants will fear.
Chassis swaps: heavy for a tank-hunter build, more armor, fewer slots. Light for speed and firepower. Medium if you can't decide. I recommend medium for beginners.
Engine upgrades increase your carry weight and speed. Cooling systems let you fire energy weapons without melting your own barrel. Don't skip on cooling.
Weapon mounts: cannons for punch, machine guns for suppression, missiles for range. Balance your loadout—overgun and your engine stalls mid-fight.
There's a tank depot here. Store backup vehicles, switch rigs between missions. Smart hunters keep a light scout and a heavy bruiser.
Heard you're taking on UNIT-0. Listen: that thing's got firepower to scrap a fortress. Max out your armor plating and cooling before you go down there.
Bring me salvage from the ruins and the lab—pre-war parts beat anything we manufacture now. I'll fit them custom.
Now, what needs fixing?

crafting_npc.name: Workshop Artisan
lines: Mind the sparks. This is my workshop—salvage in, survival out.
Name'sForge. I take what the wasteland throws away and turn it into something useful. Fuel, meds, armor, weapons—if you've got the materials, I've got the know-how.
Crafting's simple: bring me the right components and enough gold for the work, and I'll make it happen. No components, no craft. The wasteland doesn't give handouts.
I can refine fuel canisters into premium fuel—burns hotter, lasts longer. I can mix med kits with energy cells for nano repair systems that fix your tank in a pinch.
If you find ancient relics out in the ruins or the swamp, bring them to me. That pre-war tech unlocks the best recipes—plasma rifles, laser cannons, fusion engines.
You can also break down spare equipment into component materials. Got a rifle you don't need? I'll strip it for parts. Waste not, want not.
Check my recipe list. If something's marked [READY], you've got what it takes. If it says [---], you're short on materials. Go find them.
Now, what can I forge for you today?

ruins_engineer.name: Ruins Engineer
lines: Careful with that. Pre-war tech doesn't forgive clumsy hands.
I'm Wrench. I set up shop in these ruins because the salvage is right outside my door. Military-grade components, just waiting to be pried from the rubble.
I do crafting and modification work. Same as the artisan in town, but I've got access to rarer materials here. Military circuitry, reinforced plating, things the town folk have never seen.
If you're hunting the Iron Titan, talk to me first. I can craft armor-piercing rounds and reinforced armor plates from the salvage scattered around these ruins.
The lab below... I've been down there. Once. The things I saw—pre-war tech beyond anything we have on the surface. If you're going down, I can craft you gear that might give you an edge.
Bring me ancient relics from the lab or the swamp. I can reverse-engineer them into weapons and engine upgrades that'll make your tank a force to be reckoned with.
Now, let's see what we can build.

treasure_cache_1.name: Hidden Cache
lines: You discover a weathered supply crate half-buried in the mountainside.

treasure_cache_2.name: Swamp Cache
lines: You spot a rusted container poking out of the muck, covered in swamp vines.

treasure_cache_3.name: Lab Cache
lines: You find an emergency armory locker, its electronic lock long since fried.
